newsitem.title: USA: Competitors may limit Starbucks price hikes.
newsitem.headline: Competitors may limit Starbucks price hikes.

text.p: Starbucks Corp.'s customers may be in for a reprieve, as any moves to raise its coffee prices may be reigned in by competitors who choose not to, the company said Wednesday.

In a quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Starbucks said its ability to raise prices further in response to higher wholesale coffee prices may be limited by competitive pressures if other major speciality coffee retailers do not raise their prices.
At the end of May, Starbucks raised its prices for the second time this year, citing soaring coffee prices on world commodity markets.
Starbucks' inability to pass through higher coffee prices in the form of higher retail prices for beans and beverages could have a material adverse effect on earnings, it said.
The Seattle-based chain also said rapid sharp decreases in the cost of green coffee could pressure it to lower its prices before realizing cost reductions in its green coffee inventory.
The company said it entered into fixed price purchase commitments in order to secure an adequate supply of quality green coffee and establish firm prices for future periods.

As of June 29, 1997, Starbucks had about $43 million in fixed price purchase commitments which, together with existing inventory, should provide an adequate supply of green coffee for the balance of fiscal 1997 and well into fiscal 1998, it said.
Starbuck's stock was up $1.25 at $38.75 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq.
